source_review.notes: Checked current or explicitly versioned official Apache Spark configuration, scheduling, monitoring, and Kubernetes documentation; Apache Flink recovery, local-state, and TaskManager memory documentation; Kubernetes node shutdown, disruption, eviction, and pod lifecycle documentation; AWS EC2 Spot interruption guidance; and Apache Hadoop YARN NodeManager documentation. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Runtime, orchestrator, and provider behaviors are attributed within their documented scope.

evidence: Reviewed worker/incarnation identity, attempt/block/state/resource inventories, validated owners, last-copy loss, removed/replacement capacity, detection/restoration times, preserved/recomputed work, fencing epoch, failure domains, and drain success.
Checked effective-loss, last-copy, recovery-latency, preservation-ratio, and exposure-rate expressions with explicit scopes and units.
Checked that worker, executor, process, container, VM, node, attempt, block owner, state copy, volume, and failure domain remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Failure suspicion and confirmed removal are intentionally separate; safe duplicate recovery relies on fencing rather than perfect failure detection.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced lost worker w1, three running tasks, last-copy block b2, surviving blocks b1/b3/b4, and three replacement slots.
Recomputed block ownership after removing w1: b1 retains w2, b3 retains w2, b4 retains w3, and b2 has no owner.
Checked examples distinguish a 200-slot replacement deficit from the independently capped 40-slot restore-heavy admission cohort.
numerical_recomputation.notes: No universal heartbeat timeout, replica count, drain deadline, replacement headroom, recovery concurrency, or failure threshold is prescribed.

evidence: Verified atomic incarnation advance plus resource-side epoch checks reject messages and commits from a returning stale worker.
Verified artifact reuse from a nonempty set of surviving complete identity/checksum-valid owners and lineage reconstruction for last-copy loss.
Verified decommission handoff reaches zero unresolved critical ownership or explicitly falls back to abrupt recovery, and bounded admission contains recovery load.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Heartbeat timeout, kill delivery, path existence, or transfer acknowledgement alone is not treated as fencing or reusable-artifact proof.

evidence: Reviewed false suspicion, late reconnect, duplicate registration, process/container/node/zonal loss, replicated and last-copy blocks, and partial migration.
Reviewed local/primary checkpoint combinations, OOM, disk/inode/PID pressure, corruption, bad image rollout, dependency outage, preemption deadlines, and quota exhaustion.
Reviewed volume force-detach risk, cold start, cleanup duplication, credential-revocation delay, resource leaks, and correlated fleet events.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Each scenario requires safe fencing and recovery, preserved verified ownership, or an explicit terminal state rather than optimistic reuse.

evidence: Traced worker/epoch, process/container/node/provider identity, registration/heartbeat, tasks, blocks, state, resources, credentials, placement, drain, replacement, and terminal decisions.
Checked exact loss inventories, surviving-owner validation, local-state secondary status, new attempt identities, winner commit, stop-assignment-before-handoff, and deadline fallback.
Checked quotas, priority, topology, anti-affinity, correlated attribution, scoped credential lifecycle, volume safety, and diagnostic retention.
invariant_checking.notes: Cache loss is performance impact; last-copy shuffle loss is recomputation impact; durable-state loss is a correctness/availability boundary.

evidence: Reviewed incarnation-fencing, artifact-availability, decommission-handoff, and capacity-containment arguments with explicit authority and durability premises.
Checked counterexamples for heartbeat-as-death, hostname reuse, kill-as-fence, blanket block invalidation, local checkpoint authority, unverified migration, CPU-idle scale-down, and force detach.
Checked injected process/OOM/eviction/reboot/partition/disk/preemption/migration/volume/stale-return/zonal failures against exact results and bounded recovery.
proof_review.notes: Membership safety, artifact preservation, state correctness, capacity recovery, and drain efficiency require separate evidence.

evidence: Audited worker, executor, process, container, node, incarnation, suspicion, failure, fencing, abrupt loss, drain, decommission, eviction, and preemption terminology.
Confirmed cache, spill, shuffle block, local checkpoint copy, durable checkpoint, persistent volume, task output, and committed result are distinguished.
Confirmed removed slots, replacement capacity, recovery region, restored progress, preserved work, recomputed work, and blast radius are separate labels.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Spark, Flink, Kubernetes, AWS, and YARN controls are not presented as identical lifecycle or durability mechanisms.

evidence: Reviewed registrations, heartbeat age, suspicion/confirmation/drain causes, affected attempts/jobs/tenants, lost/preserved/recomputed blocks and bytes, local/remote restore, capacity deficit, fencing, and drain outcomes.
Confirmed segmentation by runtime/version, image, process/container/node pool, rack/zone/provider event, workload, artifact class, cause, and observation horizon.
Confirmed worker count, executor-time exposure, correlated incidents, affected logical work, replacement latency, recovery tails, and resource leaks are separately reported.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: A successful replacement or low executor-loss count is not mislabeled as preserved work, independent failures, or end-to-end recovery.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed identity, suspicion/fencing, loss inventory, shuffle/cache/disk, local/durable state, abrupt loss, decommissioning, replacement scheduling, autoscaling, correlated failures, security, lifecycle, and verification.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable registration epochs, task/block inventories, checksum ownership, state restoration, drain deadlines, migration acknowledgement, placement and admission, rollout containment, volume fencing, credential/session retirement, exact cleanup, dashboards, and chaos tests. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from worker identity and ambiguous liveness through artifact/state impact to drain, replacement, containment, and operations. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover stale workers, replicas, OOM, local state, preemption, scale-down, correlated images, volumes, admission, and evidence.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Spark/Flink/Kubernetes/AWS/YARN maintainer, scheduler/runtime/storage/cloud/platform/SRE/security specialist, production fleet operator, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
